verdicts.why: The gloss is 'gradually intrusive', but the note casts the word as an incursion, 'force rather than the patient creep', which denies the gradual quality the gloss makes definitional and reads the aggressive-attack sense instead.
Describes offensive intrusion as a settled trait and contrasts it with the single act of meddling; stays inside the word and the negative charge fits.
Condemns the intrusive deed in progress against meddlesome's character; matches the gloss and stays inside the word.
Register contrast with busybodied and the same charge of offensive meddling; example fits and the note stays inside the word.
Frames the intrusion as a line crossed without permission, which is the gloss's 'without right or permission'; the contrast with encroaching is about how openly the wrong is named.
A quantity past the mark, measured not judged; agrees with the gloss and the neutral label.
Beyond the requirement but simply available, contrasted with superfluous; both examples fit and the note stays inside the word.
Not needed and nothing justified it, which is exactly 'unnecessary and unwarranted' at full strength; negative charge fits.
Withholds only the claim of strict necessity, matching 'not absolutely necessary'; neutral label is plausible.
Unwarranted with the sting of waste, softer than gratuitous; example fits and charge is negative.
Surplus treated as serving no purpose, sharper than excess; examples fit and negative charge is plausible.
Surplus held in reserve and usable; matches the gloss, example fits, neutral charge is right.
Formal, weighty, beyond what was required; register note is fine and the example fits.
Dismissive surplus that could be stripped away with nothing lost; agrees with gloss and negative label.
Outside the number required without a verdict; positional and neutral, examples fit.
Amount left over as a balance, no complaint; matches gloss and neutral label, example fits.
A rebuke that says the thing overstepped, contrasted with plain unnecessary; fits 'unnecessary and unwarranted'.
States the thing was not needed with reproach implied; a mild negative charge is plausible for the gloss.
Flat absence of need without the faint blame of unnecessary; neutral label fits.
Praise by absence on a record, narrower than perfect; examples fit the record sense.
Takes in impurity as well as flaw and blemish, so it applies to substances too; examples fit.
Errorless familiarity as something drilled, contrasted with errorless; example fits this sense.
Every necessary quality present, nothing missing rather than nothing wrong; matches the gloss's 'having all necessary qualities'.
Formal, superlative accolade for the same total sufficiency; examples fit.
Perfect understanding stated flatly; matches 'understood perfectly' and the example.
Tightens down into exactness; stays with the gloss and inside the word.
A flat count of no errors, coolest beside impeccable; matches gloss and example.
Fault as well as error, so conduct as well as execution; agrees with the gloss.
One flaw undoes it, contrasted with complete's test of presence; fits the gloss.
Absence of fault as something untouched, admiring; examples fit.
Absence of fault as a standard held to, admiration over measurement; example fits.
Faultlessness kept intact, stiffer register than faultless; stays inside the word.
Perfect understanding as an attainment, contrasted with down; matches the gloss.
Completeness of its kind plus absence of blemish, contrasted with flawless; examples fit.
Plain negation without flawless's admiration; agrees with the gloss.
Plain unheated name for impatience or anger; matches the gloss and negative label.
Register label plus patience gone by erosion, contrasted with steamed; fits 'out of patience'.
British, deflating, a full loss of patience too offhand to shout; fits the gloss.
Strong distaste from having had too much, the surfeit sense the gloss names; example fits.
Absence of pleasure shown without heat; neutral-in-family is plausible for the head term.
Annoyance carried until patience is spent, contrasted with annoyed; examples fit.
Friction rubbing on rather than a single sting; same impatience or anger as the gloss.
Light, diminishing, sizes the anger as small; stays inside the word and the gloss.
Prickled and smarting, sharper than annoyed, briefer than irritated; example fits.
Small, faintly comic grievance; matches the gloss and the example.
Vulgar and blunt, coarsest register in the family; example fits the anger sense rather than the drunk one.
Coarse charge with the particle adding outward follow-through; stays inside the word.
Anger as something worked into someone; matches 'aroused to' and the example.
